title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2610.36625v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sparse event responses produce uneven keypoint errors whose effects on spacecraft pose depend on correspondence geometry and the reliability of successive observations. We present a reliability-aware framework connecting polarity--time localization, geometric recovery, event--CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization. A three-branch representation combines positive events, negative events, and recent-event timing through cross-branch attention and gating, followed by spatiotemporal aggregation. An ordered semantic-point head estimates relative correspondence precision for geometrically constrained pose recovery. Event-edge and CAD-projection agreement then guide local pose refinement under keypoint-geometry safeguards. At the sequence level, a ten-dimensional descriptor combines heatmap shape, reprojection consistency, and geometric conditioning to set time-aligned observation scales. tldr: 该论文提出一个可靠性感知的航天器位姿估计框架，通过极性-时间三支路事件表示、有序语义点精度估计和序列级观测尺度设定，将事件定位、几何恢复与CAD细化相结合，在SPADES挑战赛上实现了更鲁棒准确的位姿估计。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a reliability-aware framework for event-based spacecraft pose estimation that integrates polarity–time three-branch event representation, ordered semantic-point precision estimation, and sequence-level observation scaling, combining event localization, geometric recovery, and CAD refinement for more robust and accurate pose estimation on the SPADES challenge benchmark.
